chapter: Art Hodes, Bechet and Blue Note
title: Hodes trio at the Village Vanguard; Blue Note sessions
summary: With Hodes and Kaminsky at the Vanguard; recorded Blues and Booze, getting two percent royalties.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Where did you join Art Hodes? You joined him in New York?
Who did he have with him at the time that you joined him?
Was Max with him, Max Kaminsky?
Or was he just forming a group at that time?

No, that was for Blue Note... Max Kaminsky and myself, we was working at clubs down in the Village, Tenth Street and Seventh Avenue, the Village Vanguard -- we was working down there. Just a trio, myself and Max Kaminsky and Art Hodes. So during that time, we got a chance to record. When we recorded we used, I think, Sandy Williams on some of them... It was a five-piece band...

After we left the Village Vanguard, just where we went then, I don't know. But we did our recording first for Blue Note. During that time, we recorded "Blues and Booze." I got royalties on that record for about...oh, I guess I'd say
two or three years -- 2 percent or something.
Let's see, "Blues and Booze." We've got here Max Kaminsky with Art Hodes and yourself. There's "Eccentric," "Draggin' the Blues" or "KMH Drag," "The Draggin' Blues"...
Yeah. It's got Max Kaminsky on that one.
